oil.summary: Crude sold off sharply on Monday — WTI -2.10% to $85.23 and Brent -2.18% to $92.33 — as Iran's threat to halt Strait of Hormuz flows paradoxically triggered demand-destruction fears rather than a sustained risk premium. Iran blacklisted 45 tankers carrying oil, LNG, LPG and products, threatening fines and cargo confiscation, while one headline referenced Brent briefly surging past $100 on a Hormuz blockade scenario before retreating. The US temporarily eased Russia oil sanctions to dampen the price spike, riling European allies, even as Rystad Energy cut its Russian crude output forecast to 8.95 million bpd for 2026 amid sanctions and ongoing Ukrainian drone strikes on refineries. RBOB gasoline cratered -11.18% on the day and -12.44% on the month, the sharpest move across the complex, suggesting demand-side pressure is overwhelming the geopolitical bid. TotalEnergies announced investment in two Hormuz-bypass pipelines via Abu Dhabi's Fujairah route.
drivers: Iran blacklists 45 tankers and threatens Hormuz closure, injecting acute transit risk but also demand-destruction fears that weighed on outright prices
US grants temporary Russia sanctions relief to cap prices, offsetting Rystad's cut to Russian output forecast of 8.95 mb/d amid drone strikes on refineries
RBOB gasoline -11.18% on the day leads the complex lower; TotalEnergies commits to Hormuz-bypass pipeline investment as infrastructure hedge

gas.summary: European gas surged, with TTF settling at 68.41 €/MWh, up +3.86% on the day and +10.77% on the week, as the Hormuz standoff amplified LNG supply anxiety. Goldman Sachs warned that European gas prices need to rise further by December for storage to reach adequate winter levels if the Hormuz crisis persists — a signal that current levels may still be insufficient. Iran's blacklisting of LNG and LPG tankers compounds the supply overhang. Japan's day-ahead power prices hit their highest since January 2023, up 20% in a week, citing gas supply disruptions, pointing to Asia competing aggressively for the same LNG cargoes. On the supply side, Equinor and Aker BP reported a new gas and condensate discovery near the Balder field in the North Sea, while Norway simultaneously warned that domestic output could decline steeply post-2030 if new resource replacement lags current production rates. Henry Hub added +2.13% to $2.832/MMBtu.
drivers: Goldman Sachs flags European storage shortfall risk if Hormuz crisis persists, supporting TTF's +10.77% weekly rally
Iran blacklists LNG and LPG tankers alongside crude, directly threatening seaborne gas trade through the strait
Asia-Europe LNG competition intensifies as Japan power prices hit a 3-year high on gas supply disruptions; North Sea discovery by Equinor/Aker BP offers limited near-term relief

power.summary: The power and carbon complex tightened alongside gas, with EU EUAs gaining +1.35% to $79.56/EUA, extending a +2.78% weekly advance. The move is consistent with higher TTF gas prices forcing more carbon-intensive generation onto the grid across Europe, lifting carbon demand. Japan's power market provided the starkest signal globally — day-ahead prices jumped 20% in a week to their highest level since January 2023, explicitly attributed to gas supply disruptions tied to the Hormuz standoff. On the geopolitical backdrop, the 60-day US-Iran peace window closed on August 17, with reports that Trump's Iran strategy may shift materially, keeping tail risks elevated for energy infrastructure. European leaders gathering in Kyiv to discuss air defense support add another layer of geopolitical uncertainty that continues to underpin European power and carbon valuations. Data for this sector is otherwise limited to macro geopolitical flow-through rather than dedicated power-market headlines.
drivers: EU EUAs +1.35% on the day as elevated TTF gas prices incentivise carbon-intensive power generation and lift allowance demand
Japan day-ahead power +20% in one week to highest since January 2023, driven by gas supply disruptions linked to the Hormuz crisis
Closure of the 60-day US-Iran peace window raises risk of further escalation, sustaining the geopolitical premium across European power and carbon markets
